To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SoC-level co-design of a mobile machine learning system can improve the system-level energy efficiency by up to 2x, and the system-level throughput by up to 3x, compared to the state-of-the-art SoC designs.

(1) The design space of a SoC is much more complex than that of a standalone accelerator, (2) The design of a SoC requires the consideration of multiple components, including the camera sensor, ISP, memory, and NN accelerators, and (3) The design space is large, with a large number of design parameters.

(1) the performance of the machine learning hardware can be improved by considering the entire SoC, not just the machine learning accelerators; (2) this is especially important when the hardware must support a wide range of machine learning algorithms; (3) the performance improvement can be as much as 2x, and (4) this improvement can be achieved with only 10-15% additional hardware complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions: 1) How do we co-optimize a heterogeneous SoC to achieve optimal system level efficiency?
1) How can we leverage the synergy among different SoC components to achieve optimal system efficiency?
the following questions: 1) how can we design a machine learning hardware that can be seamlessly integrated into the entire system?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hardware architects should design SoC for machine learning applications, not just ML hardware.
hardware architects should design SoC-level optimizations to improve the efficiency of machine learning applications.
the future of machine learning hardware is a systems perspective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the system-level design space for ML accelerators is much larger than what is currently considered, and that hardware designers should consider the system-level design tradeoffs when designing the hardware for machine learning.
we can achieve up to 4X speed-up in the overall end-to-end application by optimizing the entire SoC, while the speed-up is only up to 1.5X by optimizing only the ML accelerator.
the design space is huge, and the optimal design depends on many factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hardware architect can improve the system efficiency by a factor of 2.5x by optimizing across the entire SoC.
machine learning hardware should not be treated as a standalone component, but rather be integrated as part of a holistic SoC design.
the SoC perspective is essential for designing future machine learning SoC hardware.
